newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kiev second airport seeks $100 million investment.
newsitem.headline: Kiev second airport seeks $100 million investment.

text.p: Kiev's second airport, Zhuliany, is seeking $100 million from Western investors to complete a second terminal and renovate the existing one after the city administration failed to provide promised funds.
"Construction has stopped. We are the city's municipal airport and the city has no money to finance the project further," Zuliany's director Vasyl Mamot told Reuters on Thursday.

He said the airport was working with several potential Western investors. "We need $100 million in investments but until the talks end and a final choice of an investor is made we cannot say when construction could be completed," he said.
Mamot said the city government would guarantee a credit from the Ukrainian side.
Construction of the second runway at Kiev's international airport Borispil was halted last year because the Ukrainian government ran out of money.
Operations at Zuliany, not far from the centre of Kiev, are limited to daylight hours, with about 2,000 passengers and 30 flights daily. Its short runway is suited only for small passenger aircraft.
Zhuliany serves a few international flights to Warsaw, Minsk and Bratislava and charter flights to Turkey and Bulgaria.
Ukrainian media have said the airport, built in the 1950s, is in a dangerous location, but Mamot denied this.
He said the central location could one day attract business travellers with executive jets. Quieter new-generation planes would alleviate existing noise problems.
"After finishing with the new terminal, we will renovate the existing terminal into a small business airport for six- to eight-person executive jets," said Mamot.
